text:
Paul: Quick sync — customer asks keep coming: some want messages-style chat, others prefer prompt-style completions for cost reasons. We need a clear roadmap decision and launch criteria covering roles (system/user/assistant), function/tool calling, and structured output. Where do we land?

Anya: My take: make messages the canonical public surface. It maps to role semantics (system/assistant/user) and is friendlier for function calling and structured responses. But we should provide a lightweight prompt-compat shim so clients can migrate easily.

Devon: Runtime notes: messages enable smarter prefix/KV caching which helps latency for long conversations. Prompt mode can be batched more aggressively but loses role metadata that a lot of customers rely on. Supporting both increases testing & docs burden.

Sam: From customers I've talked to (enterprise & mid-market), the ask list is: 1) enforceable system role (immutable system prompts), 2) tool calling hooks with explicit function schemas, 3) structured output enforcement (JSON schema). Launch hits if we don't provide those.

Maria: For structured output + tool calling, we need a first-class response_format contract. Proposal: add optional field `response_format`: "json_schema:v1" and `functions` array with name/signature. Runtime will validate the model response against the schema and surface parse errors to callers.

Paul: That sounds good. What are the minimal launch criteria we can commit to for hosted API?

Anya: Minimal list: - Messages-first payload (roles + content) implemented in SDK and REST - System role support with admin pinning - Basic functions spec and function calling plumbing - Schema-based structured-output validation (opt-in) - Docs + migration guide + 3 sample apps

Devon: Add infra SLOs: 95p latency under target model baseline, canary rollout mechanism, and automated fallback to compatible model variant if a model fails schema validation. Plus tests for prefix caching correctness.

Sam: Also need customer-facing acceptance criteria: two pilot customers (one PLG startup, one enterprise) agree on behavior, and no regression in quality metrics on our eval set.

Maria: Migration plan idea: accept both shapes for 6 months. Detect by header `X-RW-Input-Format: messages|prompt`. If absent, default to messages. Provide deprecation warnings in responses when prompt mode is used.

Devon: Implementation risk: dual-shape support means doubling e2e paths — recommend feature-flagged rollout: messages-only in beta, prompt-compat behind a flag, toggle for customers.

Paul: Prioritization: proposed quarter plan: Q1 - messages-first API + system pin + basic functions calling; Q2 - schema validation + prompt-compat shim + SDKs; Q3 - migrations, enterprise pilot, SLA upgrades. Agree?

Anya: Agree with prioritization, but push schema validation earlier if customers need strict contracts.

Sam: +1 to moving schema validation up if we can scope it to opt-in. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary for messages-api v1 started in us-west-2 (build 2026.04.12-rc3).

Paul: Action items: 1) I'll draft an RFC with the two-phase plan and attach proposed launch criteria; 2) @Anya and @Devon do a runtime impact assessment and estimate effort; 3) @Maria write schema validation prototype and example; 4) @Sam line up pilot customers. I'll add to roadmap board by EOD.

Anya: Will do.

Devon: I'll start infra estimate today.

Sam: On it — can ping a couple customers tomorrow.

Maria: I'll drop a prototype and short explainer in this thread this week.

Paul: Thanks — keeping scope tight is critical. If anyone sees a blocker for opt-in schema validation in Q1, call it out in the RFC.

Anya: noted.

Devon: minor comment: add an automatic metrics hook for schema failures so product can measure adoption/errors by customer.

Paul: Good call — will include in RFC.

ops-bot: reminder: weekly product sync tomorrow 10:30am.
